reviewBasis: Read directly from the frozen source's own plain text (markup stripped with no section-segmentation logic applied) and cross-checked against the raw HTML markup, using the same auditable-script method validated on chapters 105 and 183: every ... run matching a bare section-number-plus-heading pattern was extracted directly from the frozen source, independent of parse_ors_chapter.py. All 176 resulting operative catchlines were cross-checked against the chapter's own printed table of contents -- 176/176 matched, zero extra, zero missing. The remaining 95 sections omitted from the table of contents (this chapter's heavy 1970s-1999 renumbering history, largely from the 1999 c.351 licensing-law recodification) were found by a second script pass over the body text for bare section numbers immediately followed by a bracketed legislative-history citation, then classified repealed vs. renumbered (with destination number) by which keyword appears inside that section's own bracket -- including two sections renumbered out of this chapter entirely, into chapter 474 (471.502 to 474.105, 471.503 to 474.115).

methodology.catchlineExtractionMethod: auditable script over raw <b> markup, not parse_ors_chapter.py
methodology.stubDetectionMethod: auditable script matching bare section number + bracketed legislative-history citation, classified repealed/renumbered by keyword

unrelatedFindingsDuringReview.note: Comparing the parser's real output on this frozen source against this review surfaced a separate, pre-existing gap outside increment 5's own scope: ors_credits.py (increment 3, marked done) reports 4 unparsedCreditSegments for this chapter, against its own zero-tolerance gate. None of the 4 affect any field this review checks (section_number, catchline, status, renumbered_to all matched exactly, 271/271) -- they are malformed ors_source_credit citation forms this chapter's age exposed: a 'cor.' (corrective session) citation with no existing schema representation ('1983 cor. c.736 §1' on 471.410), a second citation joined by 'and by' rather than 'and' ('repealed by 1979 c.43 §1 and by 1979 c.190 §431' on 471.420), a bare non-citation predecessor reference in a form this module does not yet recognize ('enacted in lieu of 471.665 in 1997' on 471.666), and two full citations printed back to back with no semicolon between them, the first also using the plural 'amendments by' rather than 'Amended by' ('amendments by 2002 s.s.1 c.11 §1 repealed by 2002 s.s.2 c.1 §3' on 471.750). Left unfixed here rather than resolved inline: the 'cor.' form needs a schema decision (SCHEMA.md's ors_source_credit has no corrective-session column) this review is not positioned to make, and the missing-semicolon form needs a general multi-citation splitter this single example does not yet justify designing. Recorded here as a real, reproducible finding for increment 3 follow-up, not acted on.
